messages.subject: gpcount - fitted distribution is bimodal?
parts:
Greetings unmarked group, 

I have been using gpcount to examine variation in the abundance of marsh birds in two regions. I have data for 2-3 visits within a breeding season to about 9,000 sites over a 8 year period. Our surveys include 3 "intervals" within a count, one of which is a playback interval. 
I have included different combos of covariates, such as date, date2, region, time, weather variable, etc to include in the candidate models. The first thing I did was fit a global model and examine goodness of fit stats using parboot.
For a number of species, there was a lack of fit (P>0.001). So I visually inspected the fitted and observed distributions and found that the fitted distributions appeared bimodal.
And I found out that this was caused by the overwhelming effect of the playback interval, which substantially increases p. 
My original thinking was that I should include interval in the model so that I look at the effect of other variables, but I'm not sure if it is reasonable to remove it, when I know it has such as large effect. Has anybody ever had an issue like this? Any ideas to remedy the situation? 
Thanks
Myles

messages.author: b655697c64cc729d
messages.subject: Re: gpcount - fitted distribution is bimodal?
parts: I should also mention that the observed distribution of counts is very zero inflated and I used NB distribution to fit the models.

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: gpcount - fitted distribution is bimodal?
parts:
Hi Myles, can you post a snippet of output from your global model?

I'm a little confused about the problem.  You're saying there is a lack of fit in the global model which you think is caused by the playback interval.  Is playback interval a covariate in the detection model?  How does the fit change when it is included/excluded as a detection covariate?  I agree that if interval explains significant variation in detection, it should be included.  The zero inflation might be the real source of your problem here.
